newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-JAPANESE PITCHER IRABU THREATENS TO SIT OUT SEASON.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-JAPANESE PITCHER IRABU THREATENS TO SIT OUT SEASON.

text.p: Japanese pitching star Hideki Arabu is threatening to sit out the season if the San Diego Padres fail to work out a deal that will allow him to play for the New York Yankees.
Irabu's agent, Don Nomura, sent a memo to all major league clubs Tuesday expressing the Japanese ace's desire to play only for the World Series champions.
The pitcher threatened to sit out the 1997 season and declare himself a free agent next January if a trade to the Yankees was not completed by March 18.
Nomura stated that Irabu has wanted to play for the Yankees since he was a young boy and would return to Japan if he does not get his wish.
Baseball's Executive Council ruled last month that the Padres own the major-league rights to Irabu as a result of the club's working agreement with Irabu's Japanese team, the Chiba Lotte Marines.

Padres president Larry Lucchino acknowledged receipt of the memo, but said it would not deter him from negotiating with other teams. The Yankees so far have been unable to work out a deal for Irabu's services that satisfied the Padres.
The New York Mets, Baltimore Orioles, Toronto Blue Jays and Seattle Mariners have all reportedly expressed interest in signing Irabu.
Irabu, who was 12-6 and led the Japanese Pacific League with a 2.40 ERA last season, has stated numerous times that the only major league team he is willing to play for is the Yankees.
